newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES TO START BOND ISSUE BY NOV 20.
newsitem.headline: UES TO START BOND ISSUE BY NOV 20.

text.p: Russian national electricity company UES will begin issuing bonds convertible into up to five percent of shares by November 20, the company said on Friday in an application to take part in a tender for a financial advisor.

"The issue of a first tranche of convertible bonds must be completed by November 20, 1997," the statement said. "The volume of shares for conversion may be up to five percent of total RAO UES company shares."

"The bond issue may be backed with a combination of government-owned stock, UES treasury stock, and stock approved by the UES general meeting but not yet issued," UES chief executive Boris Brevnov wrote in a cover letter to the application.
Brevnov wrote that Unified Energy System (UES), Russia's largest company by market capitalisation, would choose an advisor by August 25 and accept proposals until August 15.
The statement said one or more tranches of bonds could be issued.

UES has majority stakes in most regional electricity companies, controls a number of power stations and owns the national grid. The federal government owns 52.7 percent of UES and has said it will use up to 2.7 percent minus one share of its stake in the bond programme.
